_README: Hand-editable. Not generated by the ingest - safe to extend and reorder.
Topics map to SCRIPTURE REFS, never to outline entry ids. That inversion is
deliberate: under the refs-only data profile the outline layer is absent, and a
topic pointing at outline ids would resolve to nothing. The outline layer is an
enhancement over topics, never a dependency of them.
At runtime, when outlines ARE loaded, each ref resolves to the outline entries it
overlaps, for a richer display. See src/lib/passages.ts resolveTopicEntries().
Every ref is validated against src/data/kjv/versification.json by the topic tests.
aliases: other words people actually search with. Nobody types the label I
picked — they type "worry" or "tithing". Free to extend; search matches them
the same as the topic name.
book must be a book id (lowercase, hyphenated) exactly as used in src/data/kjv/.

topics.name: Marriage
topics.description: For couples wanting to know what God intends a marriage to be, and how to love each other well through every season of it.

refs.note: The founding text: God makes the woman, and the two become one flesh.
A call to keep desire at home and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.
Two are better than one, and a threefold cord is not quickly broken; a wedding favorite on companionship.
Love strong as death, unquenchable by many waters; the Bible's high poetry of covenant love.
Jesus roots marriage in creation: what God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
Charity suffereth long and is kind; the love passage read at most weddings and needed most in the ordinary years.
The fullest New Testament teaching on husband and wife, with Christ and the church as the pattern.
Practical counsel to wives and husbands, dwelling together as heirs of the grace of life.

topics.name: Divorce
topics.description: For anyone facing a broken or ending marriage, wanting to know what Scripture actually says and where God's mercy meets them.

refs.note: The Mosaic bill of divorcement, the law Jesus and the Pharisees later debate.
For the forsaken: thy Maker is thine husband, and with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee.
God's grief over broken covenants: he hateth putting away, and none is to deal treacherously against the wife of his youth.
Jesus' word on divorce in the Sermon on the Mount.
The central teaching passage: from the beginning it was not so, with the exception clause.
The parallel account, applying the same standard to husband and wife alike.
Paul on how long the marriage bond legally binds, often consulted on remarriage.
Pastoral instruction for separation and for a believer married to an unbeliever who departs.

topics.name: Money
topics.description: For when finances have a grip on your heart - what wealth can and cannot do, and how to hold it with an open hand.

refs.note: Warns against the drift of prosperity - forgetting that it was God who gave the power to get wealth.
The foundational call to honor the Lord with your substance and the firstfruits of your increase.
Agur's prayer for neither poverty nor riches - honest about money's spiritual danger at both extremes.
He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver - names the restlessness that more money never cures.
The tithe passage - God's invitation to prove Him with our giving.
Jesus' central teaching: treasure in heaven, the heart following the treasure, and the impossibility of serving God and mammon.
The parable of the rich fool - a life measured by barns, and the night the soul is required.
Godliness with contentment is great gain, and the love of money as the root of all evil.
Be content with such things as ye have, anchored in the promise never to be forsaken.

topics.name: Debt
topics.description: For anyone carrying what they owe - the weight of borrowing, the mercy of release, and the debt already forgiven at the cross.

refs.note: God's command to relieve a struggling brother and take no usury of him - debt was never meant to crush a neighbor.
The year of release: every seventh year the creditor lets the debt go - God builds a fresh start into the calendar.
The widow whose creditor came for her two sons - God provides through the little she still had in the house, and she pays the debt.
A community debt crisis confronted head-on, with lands, vineyards, and exacted interest restored to the borrowers.
Urgent counsel on suretyship and pledged security - get free of it like a bird from the hand of the fowler.
The borrower is servant to the lender - the plainest verse on why debt costs more than money.
The unforgiving servant - an unpayable debt cancelled, and what that forgiveness demands of us.
Render to all their dues; owe no man any thing but love - the Christian's standard for obligations.
The handwriting of ordinances against us blotted out and nailed to the cross - the debt that mattered most, paid.

topics.name: Generosity
topics.description: For the question of what to do with what you have - giving that is cheerful, quiet, and unafraid of running out.

refs.note: Open thine hand wide - a warning against the grudging heart whose eye is evil against a poor brother.
There is that scattereth and yet increaseth - the liberal soul shall be made fat.
Give in secret, without sounding a trumpet - Jesus guards generosity from becoming performance.
The widow's two mites - Jesus measures the gift by what is left, not by what is given.
Lend hoping for nothing again; give, and it shall be given unto you - good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over.
Paul's farewell, remembering the words of Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive.
The Macedonians gave out of deep poverty, following the Lord who became poor to make us rich.
God loveth a cheerful giver, and is able to make all grace abound toward you.
Charge the rich to be ready to distribute, laying up a good foundation and laying hold on eternal life.

topics.name: Anxiety
topics.description: For the nights your mind will not stop circling - worry about money, health, tomorrow - and you need somewhere to set it down.

refs.note: Be careful for nothing, but in every thing by prayer let your requests be made known - and the peace of God shall keep your hearts and minds.
Jesus on worry: the birds, the lilies, and the command to take no thought for the morrow.
Casting all your care upon him, for he careth for you - the shortest place to put the weight down.
Evening, morning, and noon he cries out, and ends with: cast thy burden upon the LORD, and he shall sustain thee.
In the multitude of my thoughts within me thy comforts delight my soul - anxiety named exactly as it feels.
Perfect peace promised to the mind that stays itself on God rather than on the outcome.
Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things - Jesus gently naming an anxious heart and calling it to one thing.
Heaviness in the heart maketh it stoop, but a good word maketh it glad - why a kind word matters so much to the anxious.

topics.name: Fear
topics.description: For when something real is threatening you and you need to hear that God is present, and closer than the danger.

refs.note: Fear thou not, for I am with thee - God's own hand upholding, repeated until it lands.
The shepherd psalm: I will fear no evil, for thou art with me - the passage handed to people at hospital bedsides.
The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? Confidence spoken out loud in the middle of threat.
A very present help in trouble, though the earth be removed - and at its height, Be still, and know that I am God.
Be strong and of a good courage - courage commanded to a man facing a task far bigger than himself.
He will not fail thee, nor forsake thee - the promise underneath every 'fear not' in scripture.
God hath not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
Perfect love casteth out fear - for the fear of judgment, of not being accepted, of God himself.
The storm on the lake: the disciples terrified, Christ asleep, and the wind and sea obeying him.

topics.name: Depression
topics.description: For the long grey stretch when you cannot pray or get up, and you need to know scripture has been down there too.

refs.note: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? A man talking to his own downcast heart and telling it to hope in God.
The psalm that never resolves - it ends in darkness. Precious to anyone told they should feel better by now.
The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart, and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
He brought me up out of an horrible pit and set my feet upon a rock - the testimony of someone who came back up.
Elijah under the juniper tree asking to die - and God's first answer is food, sleep, and an angel's touch.
His compassions fail not; they are new every morning - hope deliberately recalled in the middle of grief.
Beauty for ashes, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness - from the scroll Jesus opened and read of himself at Nazareth.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
Paul pressed out of measure, despairing even of life - and God, the Father of mercies, comforting him through it.

topics.name: Grief
topics.description: For when you have lost someone and need to hear that God stays close to the broken-hearted.

refs.note: The shepherd psalm read at nearly every funeral; God walks with us through the dark valley.
The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart, and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
One line to hold onto: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
Honest grief that turns, mid-sentence, to mercies new every morning.
Comfort for all that mourn; beauty for ashes, the garment of praise for heaviness.
Jesus calls mourners blessed and promises they will be comforted.
Jesus weeps on his way to Lazarus's tomb; God does not stand at a distance from our sorrow.
The God of all comfort, who comforts us so we can comfort others.
We sorrow, but not as those who have no hope; the classic graveside text.

topics.name: Death
topics.description: For facing your own mortality or a loved one's, and what Scripture promises lies beyond it.

refs.note: Where death entered: dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
Job's confession from the ash heap: I know that my redeemer liveth.
A funeral psalm on the shortness of life and the prayer to number our days.
A time to be born and a time to die; death set inside God's ordered seasons.
I am the resurrection and the life, spoken to a sister whose brother lies in the tomb.
Let not your heart be troubled; in my Father's house are many mansions.
The resurrection chapter's close: O death, where is thy sting?
It is appointed unto men once to die, and after this the judgment.
No more death, neither sorrow nor crying; God wipes away all tears.

topics.name: Parenting
topics.description: For mothers and fathers asking how to raise, discipline, and pray their children toward God without losing heart.

refs.note: Teach them diligently unto thy children; faith passed on in the ordinary hours of the day.
Hannah lends Samuel to the Lord as long as he liveth; the text behind every child dedication.
Like as a father pitieth his children; God's own fathering is the model for ours.
Train up a child in the way he should go; the proverb parents return to most.
On correction and its fruit: a child left to himself bringeth his mother to shame.
The waiting father runs to meet the prodigal; comfort for parents of a wayward child.
Children obey, and fathers provoke not, but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
Faith handed down through Lois and Eunice; the long reward of a believing home.

topics.name: Children
topics.description: For seeing children as God sees them - given, known, welcomed by Jesus - including when a child is lost.

refs.note: The boy Samuel hears God and answers, Speak; for thy servant heareth.
David after the death of his infant: I shall go to him, but he shall not return to me. Handed to grieving parents.
Children are an heritage of the LORD and the fruit of the womb is his reward.
God covered each child in the womb, fearfully and wonderfully made, with all their days written in his book.
A child's own calling to hear a father's instruction and keep a mother's law.
The promise parents pray back to God: all thy children shall be taught of the LORD.
Become as little children to enter the kingdom, and the warning against offending one of these little ones.
Suffer the little children to come unto me; Jesus takes them in his arms and blesses them.

topics.name: Singleness
topics.description: For the unmarried season — whether chosen, waiting, or grieved — and the worth God gives a life that stands alone before Him.

refs.note: God Himself as the portion and cup; the lines fallen in pleasant places — contentment when the life you have is not the one you pictured.
God setteth the solitary in families — the promise that no one is left without belonging.
Sing, O barren — the Maker is thine husband. Spoken to those whose life looks empty of what everyone else has.
To the eunuch who says 'I am a dry tree,' God promises a name better than of sons and of daughters.
Jesus names singleness for the kingdom's sake as a real and honored calling, not a failure to marry.
Anna, widowed after seven years and unmarried through decades, departs not from the temple but serves God night and day — and is given the joy of speaking of the Redeemer to all who waited for Him.
Paul calls his own singleness a gift and speaks plainly to the unmarried and widows without shaming either path.
The undivided devotion the unmarried can give the Lord — freedom described as an advantage, not a consolation prize.

topics.name: Friendship
topics.description: For the friends who stay, the ones you need, and the kind of friend you are trying to become.

refs.note: Ruth to Naomi — 'whither thou goest, I will go.' A bond of choice rather than blood, and the Bible's strongest words of staying.
Jonathan's soul knit to David's; he strips off his own robe and sword. The Bible's picture of covenant friendship.
Jonathan goes to David in the wood and 'strengthened his hand in God' — what a friend does when you are hunted and afraid.
A friend loveth at all times, and a brother is born for adversity.
A friend that sticketh closer than a brother — and the reminder that friendship must be shown, not just wanted.
Iron sharpeneth iron — friends who make each other better by honest friction.
Two are better than one; woe to him that is alone when he falleth. The plainest case for not going through life solo.
Greater love hath no man than this — and Jesus calling His disciples friends rather than servants.
Restoring a friend in the spirit of meekness and bearing one another's burdens — friendship when someone has fallen.

topics.name: Forgiveness
topics.description: For when you need to be forgiven, and for the harder work of releasing someone who hurt you.

refs.note: Joseph weeps over the brothers who sold him: 'ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.' Forgiveness after real, lasting harm.
David's prayer after his worst sin — create in me a clean heart. Where to go when the guilt is your own.
As far as the east is from the west; He remembereth that we are dust. The tenderness of God toward the forgiven.
Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity — He delighteth in mercy and casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
Jesus' own commentary on the Lord's Prayer: the forgiveness we receive and the forgiveness we extend are tied together.
Seventy times seven and the parable of the unforgiving servant — the size of our debt measured against the one we are holding.
'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do' — spoken from the cross, mid-injury.
Put away bitterness; be kind, forgiving one another even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.
If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive — the verse to hand someone who cannot believe they are clean.

topics.name: Anger
topics.description: For the heat you can feel rising — what to do with it before it does damage, and what it is telling you.

refs.note: Cain's countenance falls, God warns that sin lieth at the door, and anger goes unruled into murder. Anger's trajectory shown early and plainly.
Cease from anger, and forsake wrath — for the rage that comes from watching wrongdoers prosper.
A soft answer turneth away wrath, but grievous words stir up anger. The most practical verse in a heated conversation.
He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty — self-control named as the greater strength.
God's patient question to a furious prophet: 'Doest thou well to be angry?' Anger that is sincere and still wrong.
Jesus traces murder back to contempt in the heart, and sends you to be reconciled before you bring your gift.
Avenge not yourselves; overcome evil with good. What to do with anger that wants to settle the score.
Be ye angry, and sin not; let not the sun go down upon your wrath — anger allowed, but not allowed to settle in.
Swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath — the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.

topics.name: Pride
topics.description: For when success, comparison, or being right has quietly hardened the heart — how Scripture names pride and what it costs.

refs.note: The proverb everyone knows, with its overlooked second half: better a humble spirit with the lowly than spoil with the proud.
Pride and shame arrive together; wisdom keeps company with the lowly.
The five 'I wills' of the heart that would ascend above God — the classic anatomy of pride.
'The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee' — pride's first work is self-deception, not just arrogance.
Nebuchadnezzar boasts over his great Babylon, is humbled to the field, and ends praising the King of heaven — pride's full arc in one sitting.
'When he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction' — Uzziah, the warning that strength is the dangerous season.
The Pharisee and the publican: religious pride exposed, and which man went home justified.
'The pride of life' set beside a world that is passing away.

topics.name: Humility
topics.description: Where to turn when you need the low place — the mind of Christ, and the promise that God draws near to the lowly.

refs.note: The central passage: esteeming others better, and Christ who made Himself of no reputation, obedient unto the death of the cross.
'God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble' — humble yourselves, and He shall lift you up.
Be clothed with humility, then cast all your care on Him — humility and trust are the same motion.
Offerings weighed against what God actually requires: do justly, love mercy, walk humbly with thy God.
The high and lofty One dwells with the contrite and humble spirit — where God chooses to live.
David after his fall: a broken and contrite heart God will not despise.
Christ describes His own heart as meek and lowly, and offers rest to the heavy laden.
Take the lowest room: whoever exalts himself shall be abased, and the humble exalted.
After washing their feet, Jesus explains the example — humility as something done, not felt.

topics.name: Work
topics.description: For the person wondering whether their daily labor matters to God, or whether it is only drudgery.

refs.note: Work is given before the fall — Adam is placed in the garden to tend it, so labor is a gift, not a punishment.
Thorns, sweat, and frustration: names honestly why work is hard without calling work itself evil.
The prayer to pray over a short life's labor — 'establish thou the work of our hands upon us.'
The ant and the sluggard — plain wisdom on diligence for anyone tempted to drift.
Enjoying the good of one's labor is itself the gift of God — relief for the over-driven.
Resurrection hope lands directly on the workbench: 'your labour is not in vain in the Lord.'
'Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord' — the verse that dignifies unseen and thankless work.
Paul points to his own labor night and day, then charges the idle to work quietly and the rest not to be weary in well doing.

topics.name: Calling
topics.description: For the person asking what God wants of their life, or wondering whether they were ever really chosen.

refs.note: Abram is called to leave before he is told where he is going — the pattern of every call that requires trust.
The burning bush, and God's answer to 'Who am I?' — 'Certainly I will be with thee.'
Eli teaches the boy Samuel to answer 'Speak, LORD; for thy servant heareth' — how to listen when you don't yet recognize the voice.
Vision, confession, cleansing, then 'Here am I; send me' — calling that begins with worship, not ambition.
'Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee' — the passage for those who feel too young or unequal to the task.
'Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men' — Jesus calls ordinary workers in the middle of an ordinary shift.
Called according to his purpose — assurance that the call rests on God's intent, not our performance.
'Ye see your calling, brethren' — God chooses the weak and foolish, so no one can boast.
Walking worthy of the vocation to which you are called, in humility, meekness, and patience with others.

topics.name: Rest
topics.description: For the exhausted and the restless — permission to stop, and the promise of rest that is deeper than sleep.

refs.note: God rests and blesses the seventh day — rest is written into creation before any command about it.
The Sabbath commandment, given to households and servants alike — rest as a protected gift, not a reward.
'He maketh me to lie down in green pastures... he restoreth my soul' — the shepherd's care for the depleted.
'He giveth his beloved sleep' — a direct word to the one rising early and staying up late in anxiety.
Even young men faint, but they that wait upon the LORD renew their strength.
'Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden' — the invitation handed to the weary.
Jesus tells the busy disciples to come apart and rest a while — withdrawal as obedience, not escape.
A rest that remains for the people of God — ceasing from our own works and trusting his.

topics.name: Addiction
topics.description: For when something has you in its grip and you cannot put it down — honest words about the struggle, and the promise that you can be free.

refs.note: Brought up out of the miry clay, feet set on a rock — the testimony of someone pulled out of a pit.
The Bible's most unflinching portrait of substance dependence, ending with 'I will seek it yet again.'
Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin — and the Son can make you free indeed.
Sin shall not have dominion over you — the core promise for anyone fighting a habit.
Paul names the exact experience of relapse: the thing I hate, that I do. No one is alone in it.
'And such were some of you' — a past tense that hands real hope to people in recovery.
Grace sufficient in a weakness that does not go away — for the thorn that stays.
Be not drunk with wine, but filled with the Spirit — replacement, not just abstinence.

topics.name: Temptation
topics.description: For the moment of pull, when the wrong thing looks good — how to stand, where the exit is, and who understands.

refs.note: Joseph runs. Sometimes the only faithful response to temptation is to leave the room.
Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee — the daily defense.
Jesus tempted in the wilderness and answering with Scripture — the pattern for resisting.
Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation; the spirit is willing, the flesh is weak.
No temptation but such as is common to man — and God always makes a way to escape.
A high priest tempted in all points as we are — so we come boldly for help in time of need.
God tempts no one; desire conceives and brings forth sin — how it actually works, step by step.
Be sober, be vigilant — resist stedfast in the faith, knowing others face the same fight.

topics.name: Doubt
topics.description: For when faith feels thin and you are half-afraid to admit it - where honest questions get met, not scolded.

refs.note: Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief - the prayer of a man with barely enough faith, and Jesus answers it.
Thomas demands evidence, and the risen Christ offers him his hands and his side - be not faithless, but believing.
John the Baptist, in prison, sends to ask Art thou he that should come? Even the forerunner needed reassuring.
Peter sinking: wherefore didst thou doubt? - but the hand catches him before the question is asked.
Ask of God, who giveth to all men liberally and upbraideth not - wisdom offered to those who know they lack it.
My feet were almost gone - envy at the prosperous wicked, unresolved until he went into the sanctuary of God.
O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear! A prophet's complaint that God saw fit to preserve in scripture.
Why sayest thou, My way is hid from the LORD? For the worn-out doubter: they that wait shall renew their strength.
Disciples who believed not for joy - he shows his hands, eats before them, and opens the scriptures to them.

topics.name: Faith
topics.description: For when you need to keep trusting God before you can see how it turns out.

refs.note: Under the stars, with no child yet in sight, Abram believes God - and it is counted to him for righteousness, the verse Paul and James both build on.
A prophet waits on God with hard questions and hears the line the New Testament quotes again and again: the just shall live by his faith.
A desperate father's honest prayer, 'Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief' - the go-to text for faith mixed with doubt.
Jesus meets Thomas's doubts with his own wounds and blesses those who believe without seeing.
Faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God - where belief comes from when you feel you have none.
We walk by faith, not by sight - steady ground when the body itself is wearing out.
The Bible's definition of faith and the promise that God rewards those who diligently seek him.
The trying of your faith worketh patience, and God gives wisdom liberally to anyone who asks.
Faith tried with fire is more precious than gold - written to believers in real suffering.

topics.name: Prayer
topics.description: How to talk to God, what to say when you have no words, and the promise that he hears.

refs.note: Jesus' own teaching on how to pray, including the Lord's Prayer.
"Lord, teach us to pray" - persistence in asking, and a Father who gives the Holy Spirit to them that ask him.
The passage handed to an anxious person: be careful for nothing, pray about everything.
David's prayer after his sin - the model for coming back broken and honest.
When you don't know what to pray, the Spirit intercedes with groanings.
Prayer in sickness and trouble; the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man.
Pray without ceasing - prayer as a continual posture, not an event.
"If my people... shall humble themselves, and pray" - God's promise to hear and heal.
The confidence we have: he hears us when we ask according to his will.

topics.name: Fasting
topics.description: Going without food to seek God - why believers fast, how Jesus taught it, and the kind of fast God actually wants.

refs.note: Jesus assumes his followers will fast, and warns against doing it to be seen.
The fast God has chosen - loosing the bands of wickedness, feeding the hungry.
"Turn ye even to me with all your heart, and with fasting" - a call to corporate repentance.
Jesus fasts forty days in the wilderness and answers temptation with Scripture.
Why the disciples did not fast then, and when they would - the bridegroom taken away.
Esther calls a fast before risking her life - fasting before a hard decision.
A fast proclaimed at Ahava to seek a right way from God and protection for the journey.
The church fasts and prays before sending out Barnabas and Saul.

topics.name: Evangelism
topics.description: Sharing the good news - the commission Jesus gave, and how ordinary believers tell others about him.

refs.note: The Great Commission: go, teach all nations, and "lo, I am with you alway."
"Ye shall be witnesses unto me" - power from the Spirit, starting where you are.
The simple gospel to confess, and "how shall they hear without a preacher?"
Ambassadors for Christ, entrusted with the ministry of reconciliation.
Be ready always to give an answer for the hope in you, with meekness and fear.
Philip and the Ethiopian - one person, one conversation, one open Bible.
The lost sheep and lost coin - heaven's joy over one sinner who repents.
"How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings."
A reluctant messenger, a wicked city, and a God who relents when they turn.

topics.name: Church
topics.description: What the church is, why belonging to one matters, and how believers live together as one body.

refs.note: "Upon this rock I will build my church" - Christ's own promise about its foundation.
The first church: the apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers.
Of one heart and one soul - shared life and shared possessions.
One body, many members - no one is unnecessary, no one is self-sufficient.
Unity of the Spirit, and gifts given to build up the body until it grows up.
No longer strangers - fellowcitizens built together as a habitation of God.
Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together - the case for showing up.
Lively stones built into a spiritual house; a chosen generation and royal priesthood.
How good and pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.

topics.name: Leadership
topics.description: For anyone carrying responsibility for others and wondering how to bear it well.

refs.note: Jethro to Moses: 'thou wilt surely wear away' — the case for sharing the load instead of doing it all.
'Be strong and of a good courage' — the charge to a leader stepping into a role he did not choose.
The LORD looks on the heart, not the outward appearance — how God actually selects leaders.
Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people rather than riches or long life.
Nehemiah surveys the ruins quietly, then says 'let us build' — assessing honestly before rallying people.
Jesus overturns the ambition of James and John: greatness is service, and the Son of man came to serve.
After washing feet, Jesus gives the example he expects leaders to imitate.
Character, home life, and reputation outweigh talent in the qualifications for oversight.
Feed the flock willingly, not for gain, 'neither as being lords over God's heritage' — the antidote to domineering.

topics.name: Justice
topics.description: For the ache over what is wrong in the world — how God feels about oppression, and what he asks of those who follow him.

refs.note: Judge with just judgment, take no bribe — that which is altogether just shalt thou follow.
Defend the poor and fatherless; deliver them out of the hand of the wicked — God's charge to rulers.
Open thy mouth for the dumb — the call to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves.
The fast God chooses: loose the bands of wickedness, feed the hungry, house the poor.
God refuses worship from unjust hands: let judgment run down as waters.
Do justly, love mercy, walk humbly with thy God — the summary verse for this whole topic.
Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these — Christ met in the hungry and imprisoned.
Jesus opens his ministry with good news to the poor and liberty to the bruised.
Favoring the rich over the poor in the assembly is named as sin — justice inside the church.

topics.name: Poverty
topics.description: For those with empty hands, and for those who must not look away - God's nearness to the poor and His claim on how we treat them.

refs.note: Leave the corners of the field and the gleanings - provision built into the harvest for the poor and the stranger.
This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him - comfort for anyone crying out from want.
He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD, who repays what is given.
The fast God chooses: bread to the hungry, the poor brought home - then shall thy light rise in obscurity.
God's anger at those whose treading is upon the poor - seek good, and establish judgment in the gate.
Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these - Christ met in the hungry and the stranger.
Jesus in the synagogue at Nazareth: anointed to preach the gospel to the poor.
Blessed be ye poor, for yours is the kingdom of God - the first word of the Sermon on the Plain.
Against showing deference to the rich - God has chosen the poor of this world rich in faith.

topics.name: Healing
topics.description: For sickness in your body or a loved one's, and for praying honestly when you need God to restore.

refs.note: At the bitter waters of Marah God names himself: I am the LORD that healeth thee.
Naaman's leprosy cleansed when he finally does the humble thing he was told.
Bless the LORD, who forgiveth all thine iniquities and healeth all thy diseases.
He hath borne our griefs and carried our sorrows; with his stripes we are healed.
Four friends carry a man sick of the palsy to Jesus when he cannot come himself.
Twelve years of illness and failed treatments end with a touch and Go in peace.
Jesus asks a man sick thirty and eight years, Wilt thou be made whole?
The church's practice for the sick: call the elders, anoint with oil, pray in faith.
The leaves of the tree of life for the healing of the nations; healing that finally holds.

topics.name: Suffering
topics.description: For the long hard season — pain that has not lifted yet, and the God who meets you inside it.

refs.note: Job worships after catastrophic loss: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away.
A short lament that gives permission to ask How long, O LORD, and still end in trust.
When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee; presence, not rescue from the fire.
A man of sorrows and acquainted with grief; Christ suffered before us and for us.
Present sufferings weighed against coming glory, with the Spirit praying when we cannot.
Our light affliction is but for a moment; the inward man is renewed day by day.
The thorn that was not removed and the answer given instead: my grace is sufficient for thee.
Count it all joy; the trying of your faith worketh patience and finishes what God is making in us.
Do not think the fiery trial strange; suffering as a Christian is not a sign of God's absence.

topics.name: Persecution
topics.description: For when following Jesus costs you — rejection, hostility, or worse — and you need to know it was expected and it is not the end.

refs.note: 'But if not' — faithfulness that does not depend on being rescued, and a God who walks into the fire.
Blessed are they which are persecuted — Jesus calls it blessing and names the reward.
If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. Hostility is not a sign you took a wrong turn.
Stephen sees Jesus standing, and forgives his killers — the church's first martyr.
Neither persecution, nor sword, nor anything else can separate us from the love of Christ.
Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed — pressed hard, not crushed.
All that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution — plain and expected.
Think it not strange concerning the fiery trial — written to scattered believers under pressure.
To a suffering church: fear none of those things — be thou faithful unto death.

topics.name: End Times
topics.description: For when you are asking how this world ends, where the dead in Christ are, and what we are waiting for.

refs.note: Many that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake - the Old Testament's clearest word on resurrection and final deliverance.
Jesus' own account of his coming, and his warning that no man knows the day or the hour - so watch.
The sheep and the goats: the final judgment, and what it turns out to have rested on.
'I go to prepare a place for you... I will come again' - the promise read at nearly every Christian funeral.
At the last trump we shall be changed; death is swallowed up in victory.
The Lord himself shall descend and the dead in Christ shall rise first - written expressly to comfort the grieving.
The day of the Lord comes as a thief; the delay is God's longsuffering, not his forgetfulness.
A new heaven and a new earth, where God wipes away all tears and there is no more death - where it all lands.

topics.name: Salvation
topics.description: For when you want to know how a person is rescued by God, and whether it can include you.

refs.note: He was wounded for our transgressions - the clearest Old Testament picture of Christ bearing our sin in our place.
For God so loved the world - the verse most people are handed first, in its full setting.
Zacchaeus: salvation comes to a house nobody expected, because the Son of man came to seek and to save the lost.
The Philippian jailer asks 'What must I do to be saved?' and gets a direct answer.
The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life - the whole exchange in four verses.
Confess with thy mouth and believe in thine heart; whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
Dead in sins, made alive with Christ - saved by grace through faith, not of works.
Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us.

topics.name: Grace
topics.description: For when you feel you have used up God's patience and need to hear that you have not.

refs.note: God proclaims his own name to Moses: merciful and gracious, longsuffering, abundant in goodness and truth.
He has not dealt with us after our sins; as far as the east is from the west - and he remembers we are dust.
Of his fulness have all we received, and grace for grace; grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.
The prodigal son: the father sees him a great way off and runs - grace that moves before the speech is finished.
Peace with God and access into grace, because Christ died for us while we were yet sinners.
'My grace is sufficient for thee' - the answer Paul got when the thorn was not removed.
The grace of God that brings salvation also teaches us how to live - grace that changes, not excuses.
Come boldly to the throne of grace to find help in time of need, from a High Priest tempted in all points like as we are.

topics.name: Obedience
topics.description: For the moment you know what God has asked and must decide — why obedience matters more than sacrifice, and what it grows into.

refs.note: 'I have set before thee life and good, and death and evil... therefore choose life' — obedience as a daily choosing.
Observe to do all the law, meditate on it day and night — courage and obedience joined at the start of a hard assignment.
'To obey is better than sacrifice' — Saul's partial obedience named as rebellion.
The conclusion of the whole matter: fear God and keep His commandments.
The two houses — hearing and doing is the rock; hearing only is the sand.
'If ye love me, keep my commandments' — obedience rooted in love, with the Comforter promised to those who keep His word.
'We ought to obey God rather than men' — obedience when it costs standing or safety.
Christ learned obedience by the things He suffered — comfort when obeying is painful.
Be doers of the word, not hearers only, deceiving your own selves — the mirror you walk away from.

topics.name: Thankfulness
topics.description: Passages to read aloud when gratitude comes easily and when it does not — giving thanks as praise, as remembering, and as obedience.

refs.note: The short psalm of thanksgiving: enter into His gates with thanksgiving, for the LORD is good.
'Forget not all his benefits' — gratitude as deliberately counting what God has done.
'O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good' — the redeemed thanking Him after trouble and wandering.
Ten lepers healed, one turned back to give glory — the searching question, 'Where are the nine?'
Generosity overflowing in thanksgiving, closing with 'Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.'
Prayer with thanksgiving as the answer to anxiety, and the peace that guards the heart.
'And be ye thankful' — thanksgiving woven into peace, song, and everything done in His name.
'In every thing give thanks' — gratitude commanded as God's will, not waiting on good circumstances.
